blocker.summary: r466 traced the 'movie worker' cinematic stall (blocking the r454-r465 oracle shader-registry-coverage campaign) to its source without launching a new oracle route -- reanalyzed r465's already-captured log. The movie worker is a REAL guest XThread (kernel object addresses 0x82916E3C/2C/08 are guest heap addresses, not host pointers), instrumented in thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/src/kernel/xboxkrnl/xboxkrnl_threading.cpp:102-104 since the AC6_recomp submodule's very first commit (ddf7c285, April 2026, original ReXGlue authors) -- predates this entire campaign. The thread never truly blocks: KeWaitForMultipleObjects returns result=0 (immediate) on every single one of 159644 logged calls across the 573s run, a tight busy-spin rather than a real wait. Cross- referenced against render_hooks.cpp: a genuine in-engine cutscene (no XMV/FMV decode anywhere in this submodule) starts at 23:57:35, ends cleanly ~46s later at 23:58:22, then the 3D world never becomes active for the remaining 6m45s of the run while the movie worker keeps spinning. Root cause not established: which of the two wait objects stays permanently signaled, and why -- needs a live gdb session breaking on the wait's return at the exact stall moment to read the underlying XEvent/XSemaphore state, which would distinguish an incomplete host stub from an already-known limitation in the original ReXGlue/AC6_recomp code (plausible given the instrumentation's age). No build state touched this cycle -- native profile unaffected, no restoration needed. Named for r467: a live gdb session on the rexglue-oracle binary, breakpoints on xeKeSetEvent/KeWaitForMultipleObjects for the three named addresses, at the exact stall point (~23:58:22, right after cutscene end). Once resolved, the shader-registry-coverage oracle track (r454-r465) can resume. Still open, non-blocking: once the PinnedShaderRuntime wiring is judged mature, reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r462); update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path for the native profile (convenience only).
